patient.name: Sophie Tremblay
patient.chief_complaint: Progressive painful neuropathy with recent severe exacerbation following pregnancy
patient.hpi: Sophie Tremblay is a 38-year-old registered dietitian presenting 6 weeks postpartum with a severe exacerbation of peripheral neuropathy that began during her pregnancy. She had a 2-year history of slowly progressive bilateral foot burning and tingling prior to pregnancy, attributed by a prior neurologist to 'idiopathic small fiber neuropathy.' She underwent normal NCS x2 and had skin biopsy confirming moderately reduced IENFD (4.8 fibers/mm) 18 months ago. During her third trimester, her neuropathy worsened dramatically with pain reaching 9/10, and she developed progressive weakness that made walking independently difficult. Six weeks postpartum, she is unable to walk without a walker, has hand weakness (particularly left), and has severe neuropathic pain with allodynia in all four extremities. She notes her prior symptoms were 'burning small fiber' in nature, but her current weakness seems different and more severe. She reports transient patches of skin reddening and mottling on her arms and legs. She breastfed for 3 weeks but stopped due to medication requirements. She had an uncomplicated vaginal delivery. She is a dietitian and has been reviewing her own diet — she has been vegan for 8 years but takes B12 supplements. She asks about potential toxic exposures. She does not drink alcohol and takes no medications other than prenatal vitamins. Prior neurologist's note says 'idiopathic SFN, monitor.'
pmh: Idiopathic small fiber neuropathy (confirmed on skin biopsy 18 months ago — IENFD 4.8 fibers/mm)
patient.review_of_systems: Positive: severe bilateral neuropathic pain 9/10, all four extremities weakness (left worse), requires walker, skin mottling/reddening episodes (livedo reticularis appearance), prior confirmed SFN history. Negative: bowel dysfunction (constipation 3 weeks — attributed to postpartum), diplopia, dysphagia, cognitive changes.

family_history: Mother: peripheral neuropathy (type unknown, diagnosed age 45). Father: 'some kind of blood disorder' (details unknown). Paternal uncle: died of 'liver disease' in his 40s.

social_history.note: Registered dietitian, hospital-based. Married. Non-smoker. Non-drinker. Vegan 8 years (B12 supplemented). No illicit drugs. Recent postpartum (6 weeks).

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented x4. Anxious but cooperative. Normal cognition.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: CN II-XII intact. No ptosis. No diplopia. Normal facial strength.
neurological_exam.motor: Left arm: shoulder abductors 3/5, wrist extensors 3/5, hand intrinsics 3+/5. Right arm: shoulder abductors 4/5, wrist extensors 4/5. Bilateral lower extremities: hip flexors 3+/5 bilaterally, knee extensors 4/5, dorsiflexion 3/5 bilateral. Plantar flexion 4/5.
neurological_exam.sensory: Hyperalgesia and allodynia (pinprick and light touch) in bilateral extremities. Vibration markedly reduced at great toes (0 seconds — absent). Proprioception absent at toes and ankles bilaterally. Temperature sensation absent bilateral feet.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Biceps 1+ bilaterally. Patellar 1+ bilaterally. Achilles absent bilaterally.
neurological_exam.coordination: Pseudoathetosis of outstretched hands bilaterally. Heel-shin impaired. Romberg positive (falls in 3 seconds).
neurological_exam.gait: Requires walker. Ataxic, wide-based. Bilateral steppage. Sensory ataxia with pseudoathetosis — suggests DRG involvement.
neurological_exam.special_tests: Livedo reticularis on forearms and legs bilaterally (visible). Pseudoathetosis present. No Babinski. No skin thickening. No rash.

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: Hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL (H), MCV 96 fL (H), Platelets 88 K/uL (H), Peripheral smear Schistocytes 3+ on peripheral smear  (H), LDH 1,840 U/L (H), Haptoglobin <8 mg/dL (H), Total bilirubin 4.2 mg/dL (H), Direct bilirubin 0.4 mg/dL (H), Creatinine 2.8 mg/dL (H), eGFR 22 mL/min/1.73m² (H), PT/INR 1.1 / 1.0  (H), Fibrinogen 328 mg/dL (H), HbA1c 5.0 % (H), Vitamin B12 688 pg/mL (H), ANA 1:40  (H), ADAMTS13 activity 8% % (H), ADAMTS13 inhibitor POSITIVE — 2.4 Bethesda units BU/mL (H).

report.summary: SEVERELY ABNORMAL NCS/EMG. Marked axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy — acutely worsened. Pan-sensory abnormalities (both upper and lower extremity). Relatively preserved motor amplitudes vs severely reduced SNAPs suggests sensory neuronopathy/ganglionopathy component (DRG involvement from microvascular TTP). Pseudoathetosis on exam is consistent with severe DRG involvement.

motor.flag: reduced amplitude — left worse than right (asymmetry)

emg.summary: Acute-on-chronic axonal sensorimotor neuropathy with pan-sensory involvement (absent SNAPs) and mild EMG denervation. Pattern is consistent with acute TTP-mediated microvascular neuropathy superimposed on prior milder SFN history.

report.overall_impression: ACUTE SEVERE AXONAL SENSORIMOTOR POLYNEUROPATHY — consistent with TTP-mediated microvascular neuropathy. Prior SFN (IENFD 4.8 fibers/mm) may represent early or mild TTP. Acute exacerbation during/after pregnancy: ADAMTS13 deficiency was unmasked by pregnancy physiological ADAMTS13 reduction. URGENT HEMATOLOGY TRANSFER — plasma exchange must be initiated within hours.

report.summary: TPE initiated within 12 hours of TTP diagnosis. Daily TPE x 10 sessions (1 plasma volume each, with FFP replacement). Caplacizumab 10 mg IV loading dose then 10 mg SQ daily added (anti-vWF nanobody, prevents platelet microvascular thrombosis). Rituximab 375 mg/m² weekly x4 scheduled (eliminates ADAMTS13 inhibitor-producing B cells). Response monitoring: ADAMTS13 activity, platelets, LDH, schistocyte count daily.
report.day_5_response: Platelets 142 K/uL (improved from 88 to above 100 — hematological response). LDH 680 U/L (decreasing from 1840). Schistocytes 1+. ADAMTS13 activity 18% (improving). Neurological: neuropathic pain improving (6/10 from 9/10). Motor recovery early — dorsiflexion 4/5 bilateral (from 3/5).
report.interpretation: TPE + caplacizumab producing rapid hematological and early neurological response. Rituximab will eliminate inhibitor for long-term remission. Expected full neurological recovery over months as microvascular thrombosis resolves and axons regenerate.

Hereditary vs Immune TTP Differentiation.value: No pathogenic variant detected — ADAMTS13 gene normal

output.test_type: Repeat Skin Punch Biopsy — IENFD (4 months post-TPE)

report.summary: Repeat skin biopsy 4 months post-TPE: Distal leg IENFD 3.4 fibers/mm (reference >6.8 fibers/mm) — still below normal but improved from 1.8 fibers/mm during acute phase (measured on admission). Proximal thigh IENFD 6.2 fibers/mm (reference >8.4 fibers/mm) — moderately reduced but improved from near-absent levels. Small fiber re-innervation occurring.
report.interpretation: IENFD improving with TTP treatment — small fiber re-innervation is evidence that axonal regeneration is occurring. Prior 'idiopathic SFN' IENFD of 4.8 fibers/mm may have represented subclinical TTP affecting small fibers before classic presentation. Functional recovery expected to continue over 12-18 months.

output.interpretation: Abnormal values: Anti-phospholipid antibodies (APS) Negative (AChR, anti-cardiolipin, anti-beta2GP1, lupus anticoagulant)  (H).

report.summary: Repeat NCS/EMG 4 months post-TPE: Improving. Sural SNAP now present bilaterally (right 4.2 uV, left 3.8 uV — previously absent). Median motor amplitude improving bilaterally. EMG: reduced fibrillations in previously denervated muscles. Nascent MUPs (early reinnervation units) appearing in tibialis anterior. Pattern consistent with active reinnervation following recovery from acute TTP neuropathy.
report.interpretation: Progressive neurological recovery confirmed electrophysiologically. Sural SNAPs recovered from absent to detectable. Nascent MUPs indicate active reinnervation. Expected to continue improving over 12-18 months. Physical therapy and occupational therapy are essential during recovery phase.

output.query: TTP pregnancy relapse ADAMTS13 peripartum management

results.citation: Scully M et al. (2014) Pregnancy and TTP: ADAMTS13 activity monitoring. Blood 123:1-7.
results.summary: TTP has 17-25% relapse rate with subsequent pregnancy. ADAMTS13 activity decreases physiologically in second/third trimester. Recommendations: ADAMTS13 activity monitoring every 4 weeks during pregnancy; prophylactic FFP or caplacizumab if ADAMTS13 activity drops below 20%; close hematology-obstetrics co-management required.

output.interpretation: Future pregnancies carry significant TTP relapse risk (17-25%). Patient counseling: if future pregnancy desired, must have pre-conception ADAMTS13 activity confirmation of remission, monthly monitoring during pregnancy, and obstetric-hematology co-management with prophylactic plan. Caplacizumab is available for prophylaxis if ADAMTS13 activity drops.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Immune thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (iTTP) with acute TTP-mediated peripheral neuropathy, presenting as acute exacerbation of prior 'idiopathic small fiber neuropathy'
critical_actions: Check CBC STAT in postpartum patient with neuropathy exacerbation — thrombocytopenia + schistocytes = TTP
ADAMTS13 activity and inhibitor — the definitive TTP diagnostic test
Plasma exchange WITHIN HOURS — delay is fatal; TTP mortality approaches 90% without TPE
Caplacizumab for rapid microvascular thrombosis cessation (prevents organ damage while TPE removes inhibitor)
Do NOT give IVIG or steroids alone — TTP requires plasma exchange as primary treatment
contraindicated_actions: Do not attribute neuropathy worsening solely to idiopathic SFN without checking CBC and peripheral smear
Do not delay TPE for further neuropathy workup — TTP is a medical emergency requiring immediate treatment
Do not transfuse platelets in TTP without hematology guidance — platelet transfusion in TTP can worsen microvascular thrombosis
Do not miss the connection between prior 'idiopathic SFN' and TTP — small fiber neuropathy as the presenting manifestation of TTP is rare but documented

differential.key_distinguishing: Prior SFN IENFD 4.8 fibers/mm may represent mild subclinical TTP small fiber involvement; acute exacerbation with TTP criteria (schistocytes, low ADAMTS13, renal impairment) definitively indicates TTP as the etiology

HELLP: thrombocytopenia + elevated LDH + elevated transaminases in peripartum period — but transaminases are normal here; ADAMTS13 activity low (TTP not HELLP); HELLP typically resolves postpartum without TPE
ANA 1:40 (negative threshold); anti-dsDNA not elevated; no SLE organ involvement beyond neuropathy; ADAMTS13 critically low (TTP pattern, not lupus-TMA)
CIDP does not cause thrombocytopenia, schistocytes, hemolysis, or acute kidney injury; NCS shows axonal not demyelinating pattern; ADAMTS13 low is pathognomonic for TTP not CIDP

key_reasoning_points: DIAGNOSTIC PUZZLE: 'Idiopathic SFN' with acute postpartum exacerbation — the critical leap is connecting CBC abnormalities (thrombocytopenia, schistocytes) to TTP as the cause of neuropathy

TTP NEUROLOGICAL MANIFESTATIONS: Classic TTP produces neurological signs in 60-80% — typically encephalopathy, but neuropathy from endoneurial microvascular thrombosis is documented; prior SFN may have been subclinical TTP
PREGNANCY TRIGGER: ADAMTS13 activity physiologically decreases in pregnancy (cleaves vWF multimers — reduced cleavage = platelet aggregation); in iTTP, this unmasks the inhibitor and triggers relapse
MAHA TRIAD: Thrombocytopenia + schistocytes + hemolysis (low haptoglobin, elevated LDH) = microangiopathic hemolytic anemia — must check ADAMTS13 STAT
CAPLACIZUMAB: Anti-vWF nanobody that blocks vWF-platelet interaction — prevents ongoing microvascular thrombosis while TPE removes the ADAMTS13 inhibitor; reduces TTP mortality significantly
LIVEDO RETICULARIS: Skin finding from cutaneous microvascular thrombosis — in young woman with acute neuropathy + thrombocytopenia, this combination should trigger TTP workup
